text:
kevin_w: Heads up — we're seeing a burst of pod egress failures from the eastus4 GPU autoscale group. Model-serving pods returning connection errors and some TCP sessions getting dropped.

tara_oncall: Oof. Any kernel logs or dmesg showing why? Is this across all AZs in eastus4?

kevin_w: Primarily az-3 and az-4. Pasted the dmesg noise from one affected node: 
```
[ 1234.567890] nf_conntrack: table full, dropping packet.
[ 1234.567895] nf_conntrack: can't insert new entry, max 65536
[ 1234.567900] ip_conntrack: FALLBACK to notracking for 172.16.0.0/12->0.0.0.0/0
```
Also ran `conntrack -S` and see counters pegged; conntrack_count ~65536.

alex_g: Sounds like conntrack / SNAT table exhaustion rather than CPU/GPU. Our pods open many short-lived outbound connections (prefetcher + metrics sinks). Could be ephemeral port churn + NAT. Quick checks: 
```sh
sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max
cat /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_count
ss -tn sport :https | wc -l
```

maria_s: Interesting — RDMA nodes aren't showing this because pod egress there uses host-networking via SR-IOV and bypasses iptables SNAT. So it's consistent with SNAT exhaustion.

sre_lead: Actionable short-term mitigations: increase nf_conntrack_max on affected nodes; add a conntrack-tuning daemonset to rollout to eastus4; and throttle the prefetcher. Long-term: move egress off node-local SNAT (deploy per-subnet NAT gateway or use egress gateway).

kevin_w: I'll push a hotfix daemonset to set `net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=200000` and `net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_established=600` as a temporary measure. Note: hashsize resize requires module reload/reboot; we can't do that without a controlled window.

kevin_w: Example quick patch (applied via sysctl in DS):
```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: DaemonSet
metadata:
  name: conntrack-tune
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: tune
        image: busybox:1.36
        command: ["sh","-c","sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=200000; sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_established=600; sleep 3600"]
```

tara_oncall: While that's rolling, can we identify the traffic pattern? Is it many distinct 5-tuples or connections to 3rd party endpoints?

alex_g: From packet captures and our LB logs it's mostly outbound to object-storage and a couple of internal model-registry endpoints. Each request spawns ephemeral connections (no keepalive) from many pods. Two obvious fixes: enable connection pooling in the prefetcher and add HTTP keepalive so connections are reused.

maria_s: Also consider bypassing conntrack for intra-cluster pod->pod ranges where possible: set `-m conntrack --ctstate RELATED,ESTABLISHED -j ACCEPT` carefully, or use calico BPF mode which can avoid conntrack for intra-node flows. But that's a bigger config change.

sre_lead: For now: 1) roll conntrack-tune DS to eastus4 (kevin) 2) throttle prefetcher rollout / patch keepalive (platform team) 3) open ticket INC-4321 and schedule a maintenance window to reboot a subset of nodes with increased conntrack hashsize.

deploy-bot: Rollout started: conntrack-tune DS -> 12/12 nodes in eastus4-az3/az4 (triggered by kevin_w).

kevin_w: Patch applied to az-3 first, errors dropped by ~80% on that AZ within 5m. Monitoring board link: https://console.redwood.ai/mon/conntrack-eastus4 (internal).

tara_oncall: Great. Can someone follow up with a runbook item for future prevention? Add recommended sysctl defaults and notes about RDMA/SR-IOV differences.

alex_g: I'll draft a runbook and a recommended platform change: egress gateway + connection pooling + keepalive defaults for model-serving pods. Will add cost impact estimate too (NAT gateway cost vs node memory/cpu cost for conntrack).

maria_s: Closing note: this is a reminder to prefer long-lived pooled connections for high-churn workloads on our GPU fleets.

sre_lead: Thanks all — leave this thread open until the maintenance window is scheduled and the hashsize bump is validated.
